header_text: Date: 2026-08-17 | Start: 14:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Claire Mendez, Jordan Patel, Luis Ortega (Redwood) — Maya Chen, Ravi Iyer, Samir Basu (Zephyrix)
summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on benchmark delta vs Zephyrix's incumbent vendor. Redwood presented tuned runs showing lower p95 latencies and higher sustained token throughput with KV caching and quantization changes. Customer requested larger dedicated slot test (25k token workload) and SOC2/KMS docs. Agreed next steps and owners.
topics: Benchmarks: latency (p50/p95/p99) and throughput vs incumbent
KV/prefix caching and warm vs cold path
Routing/fallback policy and canary for dedicated slots
Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, VPC/private deployment
transcript:
[00:00] Claire: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh well kick off. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya: Maya here, hi.
[00:07] Ravi: Ravi, on.
[00:09] Samir: Samir.
[00:11] Jordan: Jordan from Redwood, se.
[00:13] Luis: Luis CSM.
[00:15] Claire: Cool. Agenda: well review the tuned bench results vs your baseline, go over a routing/playbook for fallbacks, security Qs, and then agree next steps.
[00:30] Ravi: that sounds good, last week we saw a big p95 gap, curious what changed in your run.
[00:36] Jordan: yeah, so short version: we changed two things — continuous batching parameters and enabled prefix KV caching for repeated dialog tokens, and we also switched to INT8 quantization profile Q2 for the transformer layers where it keeps quality. The combined effect was p95 improvement and throughput uplift.
[00:52] Maya: can you give numbers?
[00:54] Jordan: sure. On your sample workload (avg 512 tokens per request, mixed short/long tail) our baseline run last week without tuning was p95 ~210ms, throughput ~320 tokens/sec sustained on the same GPU class. After tuning: p95 ~120ms, p50 ~40ms, p99 ~420ms, sustained throughput ~430 tokens/sec. Unit pro forma token cost estimate is ~$0.0018/token vs your incumbent ~$0.0026/token in the baseline we measured.
[01:28] Ravi: ok thats a fair delta. How reproducible are those numbers?
[01:31] Jordan: 80-90% reproducible on the hosted environment; once we move to a dedicated slot and pin lane configs it gets more stable. Theres still variance on cold starts — cold path p95 still spikes to ~900ms when KV not warm. Warm paths are consistent.
[01:46] Samir: cold path is the concern for us since our workload has bursty spikes, the baseline seems to hold during spikes.
[01:52] Jordan: right so we recommend a small warm pool + fast cache priming for your traffic pattern. We can set a low-latency routing policy: primary to dedicated slot, fallback to hosted low-cost variant only if dedicated hits capacity, and a warm-up ramp before heavy windows.
[02:10] Maya: what about quantization quality? Were sensitive to hallucinations and generation quality on the clinical summaries.
[02:16] Jordan: we ran our eval set against the Q2 profile; delta in Rouge/F1 like metrics was within margin (<=1.5% on average). We can share the eval script. In practice some prompts with numeric tables were slightly noisy, we kept FP16 for the final layers and int8 for the rest to reduce that.
[02:35] Ravi: curious about kernel selection — are you swapping kernels at runtime?
[02:38] Jordan: yes, runtime will pick optimized kernels based on seq len distribution. There is a minimal recompile window but we mitigated it with warm compile cache; you see a small blip first time.
[02:47] Claire: Luis pushed the security notes into chat but do you want to run through KMS/SSO quick?
[02:52] Luis: sure — Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS via our KMS connector (we can use your Cloud KMS or HSM). Audit logs are retained per plan; enterprise plan includes 1y retention and advanced query; we also support SAML SSO + RBAC.
[03:08] Maya: do you have SOC2 cert?
[03:10] Luis: yes, SOC2 Type II, and ISO27001 summary available — Ill drop links.
[03:13] Samir: what about VPC peering and private deployments?
[03:16] Luis: private control plane with VPC peering is possible; weve done air-gapped installs — theres a bit more ops work but it meets regulated data controls.
[03:24] Ravi: back to throughput: when you say 430 tokens/sec sustained, what load shape and GPU guess?
[03:30] Jordan: thats measured on an A100-equivalent in our dedicated pool with continuous batching tuned for your 20-30 concurrent streams. The test was a 30-minute run using your traffic mix.
[03:40] Ravi: can you run a larger test? 25k token burst sim for the nightly batch job we have?
[03:44] Jordan: yes, well schedule a 25k token sustained run on a dedicated slot — we want to capture p50/p95/p99 and GPU util.
[03:50] Claire: thats one of the agreed next steps — Jordan will run that and post logs.
[03:55] Maya: also, we need to see head-to-head latency distribution against the incumbent when traffic ramps, not just averages.
[04:03] Jordan: understood. Well run a head-to-head with identical trace replay and produce CDF plots.
[04:08] Ravi: question on routing/fallback: if dedicated is full and were failing over to hosted, are tokens billed differently?
[04:13] Claire: yes, pricing tiers apply — dedicated slot commit price vs hosted on-demand. We can set a fallback that still pins model variant to a cheaper quantized variant to keep latency cost tradeoff predictable.
[04:24] Samir: any risk in fallbacks causing inconsistent output?
[04:27] Jordan: small risk if model variant changes; we use canary and automated regression evals on fallback to ensure quality doesn't degrade beyond your threshold. You can set a hard policy to stop fallback if eval delta > threshold.
[04:39] Maya: what about warm cache priming — can Redwood pre-warm the KV cache each morning?
[04:44] Jordan: yes, we can run scheduled priming jobs; cost is small relative to the p95 improvements. Well show a cost-proforma.
[04:51] Ravi: curious if your quantization profile Q2 is compatible with our legal/regulatory requirement for determinism in audit trails.
[04:58] Luis: determinism is mostly orthogonal — we can enable deterministic kernels and log seeds, plus full request/response audit logs. KMS handles key rotation for encryption at rest.
[05:10] Maya: okay good. A couple of quick clarifications: can you share the eval scripts and the raw trace of the tuned run?
[05:16] Jordan: yes well share the scripts, the run logs, and the plots. Note: there might be a couple transcription typos in the auto notes — oh sorry I mean, there might be a couple of mislabels in the run metadata but well clean them.
[05:29] Samir: One more ops asks — during the 25k token run can you capture kernel switch events and compilation latencies?
[05:35] Jordan: yes, we can instrument compile/cache hits.
[05:38] Ravi: timeline — were looking to decide by end of month for dedicated commit. Do you think results will be mature enough?
[05:43] Claire: yes, if the 25k run matches the warm-path numbers and the head-to-head CDF shows consistent p95 improvement, youll have the data to present to procurement. Pricing and SLA draft by next Tues should fit your timeline.
[05:56] Maya: great. Anything else on routing / playbook?
[05:59] Jordan: well propose a routing playbook: warm pool size, pre-warm job windows, dedicated slot thresholds for fallback, and quantization variant mapping.
[06:08] Luis: Ill attach SOC2 cert, KMS integration steps, and audit retention options to the shared folder right after.
[06:14] Claire: recap: Jordan runs 25k burn, we share head-to-head CDFs, Claire sends pricing and SLA, Luis posts security docs, Maya uploads sample traces. Next sync in one week unless you want to escalate earlier.
[06:27] Maya: thats fine. thanks.
[06:29] Claire: thanks everyone.
[06:31] [call ends]
